objective: Prove: (Lemma 1) in one stage the earliest arrival between cells is the steps to the next contact, g times the hop distance of the contact lattice (exactly 2 hops per ring step along an axis), and the steps from the last contact; (Theorem 2) for every doubling schedule from the open n x n tube (n >= 3, g >= 2), whenever T1(v) is defined, 4g d(v) - 6g <= phi(T1(v)) <= 4g d(v) + 9g + 2, and T1(v) is defined once the schedule's conformal length reaches the upper bound; (Corollary 3) the conformal round trip is within [8g d - 12g, 8g d + 18g + 4], so it satisfies the triangle inequality up to 42g + 4. Check Lemma 1 against breadth-first search and Theorem 2 against every census reading and fresh random schedules; compute that plain lags have unbounded excess.
status: Proved 2026-11-10 (by hand; Lemma 1 checked against breadth-first search on 326,400 pairs, Theorem 2 against 15,373 route arrivals): one-stage earliest arrivals are the steps to the next contact, g times the contact lattice's hop distance (two hops per ring step), and the steps from the last contact; for every doubling schedule, 4g d(v) - 6g <= phi(T1(v)) < 4g d(v) + 9g + 2 in conformal time, so the conformal round trip satisfies the triangle inequality up to 42g + 4; plain lags have unbounded excess (computed).
title: A growing plane reads taxicab distance in conformal time
